**PORTFOLIO UPDATE 7/1**

Hey guys, nasty day thanks to that META news pre-market — semis and the AI trade didn't like it and got hit hard. Not going into the reasons, it is what it is.

**Market picture**
Tape is pretty divergent here. QQQE actually not looking bad, still above a rising 21dma-structure. MCSI hooked up on QQQ — breadth extension regime attempt. Credit Spreads clean with the backtest and rejection of the declining 21dma-structure. VIX same story, good below its declining 21dma.

So the damage today was really contained to semis and AI, which happens to be the only leading group right now — and where I was heavy. So I took a pretty big hit. Part of the game.

**So all in all**, top-down the picture isn't broken at all. But the LLs took a real distribution day (-95th GDB), and that's the feedback that matters most to me right now.

**On my book**
Here's the real read: it's now three weeks since that Friday where every time I gain traction and push exposure back up, I get slammed back down at prior equity highs. That's the feedback. The market still looks like it's in that base and chop, and I don't want to get caught overweight in it.

So into the close I trimmed exposure below structure, reduced SNOW/CRWD add at 2R, and cut the weaker names. Book is back to a mature, financed core with just a thin new layer on top — NER contained, NE Δ tight, plenty of cushion to the stops. Off margin, sitting lighter with some cash on the sidelines.

From here I'm just watching. Can the tape firm up? Can we see broadening into the rest of tech? Can semis and AI stabilize, form the right side, and push to new highs? All things I'll be watching — personally a bit lighter for the next few days.

At the end of the day, you have to respect the feedback you get, despite what you're seeing or thinking of the market.

Good luck guys ✌️

**PORTFOLIO UPDATE 6/30**

Hey guys,

Back-to-back strong day, and another easy thrust on top of yesterday's reversal. For me that's the trend reconfirmation I was waiting on. Whatever happens from here — stress test, sideways, whatever — the train is back up and away from structure, even without a new high yet.

**Market picture**
QQQE followed through cleanly on yesterday's daily reversal — trend back up, pushing away from the 21dma. Breadth was actually nothing special today (-1 net adv ratio, more decliners than advancers), but momo daily ratio at 7x tells you it was a strong day in thin tape. You had to be in the leaders, and the LLs composite was the strongest read of the day — hard push on price, breadth at GDB +83, MCSI hooked up and now above 10dma.

VIX broke down from 21dma-structure. Credit spreads broke down from 21dma-structure. Both reads I've been watching for as the external confirmation — and we got them on the same day. That's clean.

Breadth ext but not OB yet. MCSI not fully hooked-up either, so there's still room.

**So all in all,** the reconfirmation is in. The job now isn't to press — it's to follow the leaders, trim into strength, and stay patient. No edge in adding here with the tape extending.

**On my book**
Game plan today was to do nothing new and instead derisk into strength on what was already working — and that's exactly what played out. DELL and MRVL both hit 2R and got trimmed 1/3, which graduates them out of NE and locks in realized on top of working cores. Great feedback on top of cores that are already doing their job.

The book is mature and mostly financed core. New layer is small, contained, and getting paid — fresh exposure has traction, the cushion is real, and there's nothing fragile about the structure underneath it. Margin is still on, but it's earned: cycle's working, follow-through is in, and the cushion absorbs anything reasonable from here. This is the productive middle — the longer the book lives, the safer it gets structurally.

CORZ was the one underperformer on the day, but I'm giving it the rest of the week to bounce off the base structure. Trimmed already, cushion in place, PF cushion gives me the patience.

Smart cycle behavior here is patience. Trim into strength, let leaders extend, don't stack fresh entries into an extended tape. Repeat the process.

Good luck guys ✌️

**PORTFOLIO UPDATE 6/29**

Hey guys — finally feels like the right day. Looks like the market needed last week to fully digest and base, and today we got the right side starting to form.

**Market picture**
QQQE confirmed a daily reversal off a higher low at the rising 21dma-structure. That's the read I've been waiting on. Powerful action across the top groups and liquid leaders — undercut & rally shakeouts, oops reversals, and Friday's high reclaimed on most of them. That's risk-on behavior off structure.

Breadth firmed up with MCO pushing higher on a +87th GDB score, and MCSI trying to curl off an oversold touch. Internals softened in the right direction — VIX range breakdown, trying to lose its own 21dma-structure too. Credit spreads still inside the 21dma-structure but printed a clean downside reversal off the 21ema — that's the one I still need to see break down tomorrow to fully sign off.

LLs tapped the 21dma-structure at open with a strong daily reversal and +82nd GDB. Just look at the top leaders — oops reversals and shakeouts at the 21dma-structure with strong action off the right side. That's continuation behavior, not distribution.

**So all in all**, the setup for continuation is here. Today's QQQE reversal is the confirmation candidate, but it has to stick — need credit spreads to follow through tomorrow.

**On my book**
I engaged today. NEW exposure on INTC, DELL, MRVL, plus an ARM add and an NBIS add. NER sits at -2.2%, which is right at my ceiling — but that's the whole point: I open the layer at structure when the tape gives me the window, not after the move's already gone.

The book is covered. NE Δ is positive, the new layer is already showing traction, FER/UER and NE/CE are all within limits, and Open Heat is contained against a fat cushion of open profit. This is exactly how I want to engage a turn — fully aware of the risk, with the rest of the portfolio doing the work underneath.

From here, my job is done on the entry side. No more fresh exposure. Patience now — trim into strength, trim into extensions, and let the layer prove itself. If the market follows through tomorrow, the fresh stuff finances the next push. If it doesn't, the cuts come from the weakest names first.

Good luck guys ✌️

NEW: INTC, DELL, MRVL

TRIMMED: INTC, NBIS

**PORTFOLIO UPDATE 6/28**

Hey guys, choppy week capped off by another weak session Friday. Saw some real rotation into software and cyber, but the semis got hit and a few of my names broke structure on me — so the day turned into a cleanup pass.

**Market picture**
QQQ traded back below the 21dma with a retest and rejection Friday — second time this week the bulls couldn't hold it. QQQE held up better, sitting right into rising 21dma structure, and short-term breadth is still oversold. So there's a potential setup developing here, no question about it.

But the other side of the tape is harder to ignore. VIX still trading above its 21dma. And credit spreads closed dead high above rising 21dma structure — that's the read I care about the most. Semis were the clear weak spot all week, software and cyber are where the strength rotated into. Weekend headlines on the Middle East de-escalation could give us a gap up Monday, remains to be seen if it holds.

**So all in all,** weekly trend is still up, we're still above rising weekly structure, and the queues are still trying to form a higher low. The setup is there. But the daily action is split and credit spreads are flagging — so Friday wasn't a day to press, it was a day to make sure the book could survive being wrong.

**On my book**
Got pushed out of a few names that broke 21dma structure — VRT closed back below, FLEX had a nasty failed breakout, BE down 18% closing below structure, CSCO same story, ARM (5/12 lot) the same. So a chunk of the cleanup was the tape forcing my hand on names that lost structure.

The bigger driver though was UER and FER. Pre-close my book was getting fragile — a lot of positions sitting close to their stops, not much open profit left to absorb a bad day. That's exactly the setup that hurt me earlier this month: too aggressive on margin with a portfolio close to its stops. Not making the same mistake twice. Even with the QQQE-into-structure setup right there, even with breadth still oversold, my job is to manage risk first — that's what keeps me in the game long term.

So I cut what was below the 21dma, trimmed ARM, kept cores even though it's below structure because the April position has enough cushion to give it the week to reclaim. Brought Total Exposure back to 80%, off margin, NER and NE Δ back in budget, NE/CE down to 0.31x. Book is mostly mature core now (ARM, NBIS legacy), fresh layer is contained.

Sleep-at-night level over the weekend, but still exposed enough that I can quickly get back to full if early-week action confirms the higher low. Day-by-day situation from here — need to see how a potential gap up gets held and whether we can build on it.

**Good luck guys ✌️**

**PORTFOLIO UPDATE 6/25**

Hey guys,

Wild tape again today — fade into the close, plenty of weakness on the screen, but at the end of the day everything is still holding structure. Classic summer chop.

**Market picture**
QQQ and QQQE still > rising 21dma-structure. Initial rejection of the reversal pivot today — tape wasn't ready, no new info gained vs yesterday. Internals refused to spike above structure, so we're back inside the chop range.

Breadth still sucks on the surface but MCO is oversold with breadth ext actually up — positive GDB, stocks reclaiming their 5dma. LLs had a good day under the hood: GDB at +80th, MCSI back in uptrend above rising 10dma, breadth expansion. Credit spreads closed nicely red, rejecting structure — that's the one I'm watching closest. As long as SHY/HYG stays capped under that level, there's no underneath red flag forcing me to IRA cash.

**So all in all,** this is fading/basing action inside a still-intact structure. Can it lead to a top? Sure. Can it also be the right side building before continuation? Also yes. The LLs holding and basing at their rising 21dma is what's keeping me on the glass-half-full side until proven otherwise.

**On my book**
No exposure adjustments at the close. VRT got derisked, OUST opened with cushion, FLEX gave me nice cushion on the NER too. The new layer is contained and starting to get paid — not the biggest cushion, but enough that I don't need to force anything.

Book is mature, UER is clean, NE Δ is in a spot I can live with. FER is elevated though — that's the one read I'm watching. A lot of names are sitting closer to their stops than I'd love after this fade, so if credit spreads break and the tape keeps fading, that number forces my hand. For now, structure is holding and the LLs are doing their job, so I'm staying patient on margin rather than cutting into weakness.

If you already have exposure, this is the spot to be patient — trim into strength, try to add into weakness right into structure on the leaders that are still working. There are some out there, but it's definitely harder to position. Less is more. Enjoy the summer. If you have cushion, let structure do the work.

Good luck guys ✌️

**PORTFOLIO UPDATE 6/24**

Hey guys, the setup was there today and it was a real one — price into support, breadth oversold, internals holding. The question wasn't whether the spot was there, it was what kind of trader you wanted to be at it.

**Market picture**

QQQE pulled right into the rising 21dma-structure and held the 21ema, with breadth washed out — MCO at -1.35σ, stocks above 5dma down to 22% (OS). LLs still above their own rising 21dma-structure and digesting, ST breadth on the OS hook-up. Five-pillars-wise, price in support, breadth oversold, internals at risk but holding right at declining 21dma-structure. The one not on board — credit spreads, SHY/HYG still below declining 21dma-structure. That's the piece still missing.

**So all in all,** the ingredients were there for a make-or-break, and MU after the close looks like it's sparking some buying in the AI trades. But ingredients aren't follow-through. Tomorrow I want to see continuation confirmed AND credit spreads rejecting structure. Until then, it's a setup, not a thrust.

Two ways to play it from here — you wait for the confirmation gap-up and accept that the leaders will already be extended off lows, or you buy into the discomfort, into the oversold, into the support, and trust your process. I leaned into the second today because the structural setup was there and I wanted to be positioned ahead of a potential catalyst, not chasing after it.

**On my book**

Book is running hot on the guardrails and I want to be straight about that — FER and NE/CE are both elevated, and we're on margin into the close. That's not a number that fell out of nowhere, it's a judgment call. The setup gave me a real spot, I'm overweight leaders that were lined up at structure, and MU was a known catalyst into the close. I made the choice to lean into that.

The fresh layer isn't being paid yet — NE Δ is sliding, which is the honest read on a day you bought into discomfort. That's the price of getting positioned ahead of the move instead of after it. Tomorrow tells me whether the lean was earned. If MU + continuation deliver and credit spreads finally crack structure, the book is in the right spot. If we get rejected here and breadth doesn't thrust, I'll be cutting back into the open — that's the deal I made with myself taking the book up to where it is.

The big VRT entry today was the cleanest expression of the thesis — been talking about it since last week, was waiting for that exact 21dma-structure backtest, and the spot came. That's a right-side entry, not a chase.

Good luck guys ✌️

QQQ down ~3% retesting the low of the 21dma-structure and the recent reversal pivot. Big spot. Market still needs to digest that big April/May run, and we might be heading into some summer chop. Wouldn't surprise me.

But the action underneath isn't that bad. Credit spreads spiked but got rejected at the declining 21dma-structure — I give that a lot of weight in my EOD process, and the rejection on a -3% QQQ day is constructive. VIX back above rising 21dma-structure but nothing extreme. LLs still above a rising 21dma-structure, MCO took a dive but not oversold yet — getting there. LLs breadth ext. washed out, LLs above their 5dma at 25%.

**So all in all**, there was real and interesting decoupling today — CRWD, CORZ, NBIS, CSCO, even the new SNOW pos. Some bad, some good. I'm choosing to focus on the good and see if the bad catches up or the good creates a buying opportunity.

**On my book:**
Two-sided day. Closed LITE which is now below structure, took MXL out of the new layer, and reduced semis exposure I had. On the other side, opened SNOW to rotate some software back in, added to ARM cores at structure, and added to FLEX. Not looking to be aggressive, but I want to remain fully invested as long as the action under the surface keeps showing me what it's showing me.

The book is healthy where it counts — fresh layer is contained, mature core is doing the heavy lifting, and nothing's tight against stops. NER, NE Δ, NE/CE, UER, FER all within parameters. That's the whole point of running the dashboard — on a day like today I don't have to wonder if I'm overextended, the numbers tell me I'm not.

Cycle posture is still productive middle. Not pressing, not retreating.

Good luck guys ✌️

Posture here is custodian, not aggressor. Patient with what I already have, let the leaders work, don't add for the sake of adding.

**PORTFOLIO UPDATE 6/16**

Hey guys, constructive digestion day. Giveback on QQQ was expected — we talked about it in EMS — and most of the names that ran to R in the last 3 days just backtested. Nothing broken.

**Market picture**
QQQ gave back as anticipated. We've almost filled the gap, and the next real spot is the rising 21dma-structure + recent swing high pivot around 720/723. That's the level I'm watching tomorrow on a red open.

Breadth cooled off — MCO back to neutral on QQQ, but LLs MCO is back oversold (!!!). VIX still tamed below 21dma-structure. Credit spreads below 21dma-structure backtesting recent swing low pivot. Five pillars still constructive.

LLs themselves — same story. AMD ran 25% in 3 days, of course it digests for a session. Backtest of the prior swing high pivot is normal action unless we start breaking structure.

**So all in all,** I see this as constructive action. No guarantees, but the setup tomorrow on a red open into structure with LLs MCO back OS is exactly the kind of spot I want to be engaged for — *if* the action confirms it.

**On my book**
- NER: -1.33% — fresh layer on but contained
- NE Δ: -0.55%
- NE/CE: 0.40x — pulled back in line after the afternoon trims
- OH: -11.33%
- UER: 17.8%
- FER: 6.4%
- Total Exposure: 94.6% — off margin, where I want to be overnight

The afternoon cuts were pure risk mngmt. Pre-close, UER was >50% and NE/CE was at 0.85x — too green, too fresh, and I was on margin without the NE delta to justify it. Closed TSLA and CLS to bring the book back in line. NOK also stopped same-day. If those new names had given me real traction and a working NE delta, different story — but that wasn't the case, so I'm not going to babysit unproven exposure on margin overnight.

Also worth flagging: FOMC tomorrow. 14:00 decision, 14:30 conference, and a new Fed chairman — could bring more vol than usual. Another reason to keep the book clean tonight and let tomorrow tell me what to do.

Stayed engaged in the weakness as opportunity (added FLEX, BE earlier in the day) but kept NE focused on strong setups only. If tomorrow we get the red open into 720/723 with decoupling and support holding, I'll push more exposure again. For now, metrics under control and waiting.

**PORTFOLIO UPDATE 6/10**

Hey guys, another rough one. High vol, more Middle East headlines, and the oversold bounce I was looking for just didn't show up. What's oversold can stay oversold — you don't fight price. Price is #1.

**Market picture**
Today QQQE broke its 21dma-structure, and MCSI accelerated lower. The one positive: MCO is now oversold, so a bounce is possible — but I have to respect price here.

QQQ and SPY both retested a declining 21dma-structure and got rejected. NYSE and Dow Jones broke their structures outright. VIX made a new high above Friday's, and credit spreads are trying to reclaim their 21dma-structure. That's a stack of red flags.

**Monthly distribution:**
Performance was not linear. A handful of strong months (APR, JUL, SEP) accounted for a large portion of the yearly gains, while losing months remained contained. This reinforces the importance of market timing and knowing when not to press.

Overall, the stats confirm that 2025 was not about trading more, predicting better, or chasing returns. It was about letting structure, R-multiples, and patience do the work, while keeping risk tightly controlled during unfavorable environments.

This is exactly the type of statistical profile I want to carry forward into 2026.

Best performance came from a limited number of high-quality market windows

This year reinforced something I’ve learned repeatedly over time: performance doesn’t come from constant activity. Most of the gains came from a handful of well-timed periods where market structure, breadth, and leadership aligned. The job was simply to be ready, patient, and appropriately sized when those windows opened — and to protect capital when they didn’t.

Consistency, risk control, and process adherence mattered far more than any single trade or month.


## PTA — 2026 Focus & Refinements
Going into 2026, the goal isn’t to trade more or take more risk. It’s to extract more from the same edge, with the same discipline, while continuing to reduce stress and decision fatigue.

**1. Carrying More Size Through Winners**
One of my main refinements for 2026 is how I handle winners after they prove themselves.

**Instead of trimming multiple times into strength (e.g. at 2R and 5R), I want to simplify the process:**
- Take one trim at 2R (⅓ of the position)
- Carry the remaining ⅔ as a true runner core
- Manage that core strictly off structure, not targets

The intent here is clear: maximize participation in the few trades that actually drive yearly performance. The stats already show that large R winners do the heavy lifting. This adjustment is about giving those trades more room to work, without increasing initial risk.

Nothing changes on entry, risk, or sizing — only on how long I stay involved once the trade has earned it.

**2. Size & Risk Per Trade — Staying Exactly Where I Am**
I’m in a very good place with position sizing and risk per trade, and I have no intention of increasing it in 2026.
- No single trade can materially damage my equity
- Drawdowns remain manageable
- Portfolio construction removes emotional pressure
- Decision-making stays clean under stress
**This balance is a feature, not a limitation. It allows me to:**
- Sit through normal volatility
- Hold winners longer
- Avoid reactionary decisions

The focus in 2026 is better utilization of size, not more size.

**3. Gap-Down Days — Mental Framework**
These all-day gap-down sessions are designed to feel worse than they are. Pressure all day, weak close… then everything gaps up the next morning.

My focus in 2026 is mental framing, not reaction.

**- Discomfort ≠ information**
Red P&L is not a signal. Structure is.

**- Goal = avoid irreversible decisions**
I’m not optimizing. I’m surviving.

**- Zoom out**
If daily structure and leadership haven’t changed, neither has the trade.

**- Resolution often comes after the close**
Forcing clarity intraday is how good positions get dumped.

**Bottom line:**
Less reaction. More observation. Trust structure.

## Wishing everyone a great 2026 — both in the markets and outside of them.
Stay healthy, stay patient, and don’t lose sight of why you’re doing this in the first place.

Plenty of opportunities ahead. Let’s approach them calmly and with intent.

Cheers,

**Introducing My "Longer-Term" Strategy**
In 2025, I initiated a longer-term strategy, which I call my "Position Account." This approach is an evolution of my current trading system, adapted to be less active while capturing bigger market trends. With work commitments growing in other projects and the realization that patience is rewarded in trend-confirmed markets, I began this adaptation at the start of the year. Going forward, I will focus exclusively on this strategy, as managing two strategies in parallel conflicts with its core principles.

**Key Features of the Longer-Term Strategy:**

**1. Same Entry Methodology:**
- Identifying leading, liquid stocks showing relative strength.
- Positioning early in larger trends, particularly during mid-to-long-term market oversold conditions.
- Buying into broad market fear but focusing on names that decouple and demonstrate strength.

**2. Scaling In:**
- 10% pilot position on anticipation.
- 5% addition at the reversal pivot.
- 5% addition on Day 2 follow-through.

**3. Holding and Selling:**
- Holding positions based on structural integrity and the 50-day moving average (50DMA), rather than the 21DMA.

**-  Selling process:**
- 33% trimmed into strength at 2xATR extension from 10dma.
- 33% trimmed  into strength at 6xATR extension from 50dma.
- 33% sold on a break below the 50DMA.

- Waiting for stocks to set up again before re-adding them to the portfolio.

**4. Portfolio Management:**
- Targeting 8-10 positions to reduce concentration risk.
- Starting with a maximum of 12 positions, reducing to 10 as the trend matures.

**Adjusting exposure:**
- 120-150% early exposure during oversold breadth conditions.
- Reducing margin when short-term breadth becomes overbought.
- Re-entering margin positions only when short-term breadth resets to oversold while maintaining mid-term breadth below overbought levels.

**5. Stock Selection Focus:**
- Prioritizing very select liquid leaders with 6-12 month relative strength.
- Shifting to Alpha Leaders with 1-3 month relative strength once the trend confirms.
- Prioritizing stock-specific action over broader indices once breadth and market conditions confirm the turn.

    - Only position when market is MT oversold after a pullback. Wait for those leaders to get into the 50dma area. Be agressive in that spot, need good size on early momentum to create cushion.
    - Use ST oversold market to add back to winners or get on margin early in a market move.

- Streamline my process with Tlab
    - Use my Alpha scan for Swing acct. & Liquid Leaders for Position acct and narrow the market to only a few leading stocks. (30-40 names per scan)
    - Use my Alpha PB scan for focuslist generation, but allow myself to use Alpha Entry Alert scan during the day to initiate trade.
    - Use my Liquid Leaders Entry Alert scan to position into leaders when market is giving that Mid or Long-term pullback opportunity or adding to positions on ST dip.

Those are the high-level strategy & trading goals for 2025, but I am working on a more extensive system document to refine those rules.

Cheers to 2024, and let's kill 2025 with a renew focus.
